title: Continuous sentence MEG: context beyond the 1 s per-word window
description: Holdout sentence npz ships continuous MEG (156,306,1030) at 250 Hz (~4.1 s incl. extra end) with word_onsets_s; our 'windows fixed at 1 s' premise holds only for the 92 isolated-word rows. d'Ascoli uses 3 s windows from onset. Lever: word encoder sees longer post-onset context (e.g. 2-3 s, clipped at sentence end) or a sentence-level conv over the continuous signal. Needs train epochs cut from continuous runs the same way. Depends on all-word caching.

title: Data coverage: use all the signal the competition gives us
description: Use all the signal the competition gives us. Our 0.385 LB vs the organisers' d'Ascoli reference at 73.23% (2609.03231 Tab1; LB top 0.765) traces to data use, not architecture. We train on 40% of sub-0 word events (vocab-only), with 1 s windows; the reference trains on all sub-0 data, and MEG-XL fine-tunes on 3 s windows from -0.5 s. Rules allow any data, including other subjects and public pretrained models (2609.03231 s2.2).
design:
ORDER (each step scored locally, then submitted at a paced slot if it beats the champion):
1. 7gf.24: continuous 50 Hz fp16 cache per run (~9 GB sub-0 on GPU); every word event with sentenceidx; spans = PNPL sentences up to 9 words; loss on in-vocab slots; all-word novel-sentence ruler; fix spans.py docstring.
2. 7gf.25.1: window length as a knob (1 -> 3 s from -0.5 s, clipped at sentence end), cut on GPU from the continuous cache.
3. 7gf.25.2: final refit on train+val at the selected epoch.
4. 7gf.25.5: subjects 1-32 (fetch --others, ~2.6 GB at 50 Hz) joint-trained with subject embeddings; LB100 Fig2 says they help sub-0 on TIMIT/MOCHA/podcast.
5. 7gf.25.3 / .25.7: OOV words as T5/SigLIP targets; phoneme/audio auxiliary heads.
6. 7gf.25.4: holdout scaler adaptation (low).
ENABLERS: 7gf.17 throughput (GPU at 12-17% util, ~5x headroom), 7gf.28 ruler noise (tiny per-class val n), 7gf.20 soup/ensemble last.
acceptance_criteria:
WORK criteria, not score criteria:
1. 7gf.24 landed: continuous 50 Hz cache for every run (all 162 sub-0 h5, closes 25.6); every word event with sentenceidx; sentence spans; loss on vocab slots; all-word novel ruler; tests + gates green.
2. 7gf.25.1 landed: window length + pre-onset offset as a config knob, cut on GPU; 1 s and 3 s arms run.
3. 7gf.25.2 landed: refit-on-train+val mode.
4. 7gf.25.5 landed: subjects 1-32 cached + joint-training path with subject layer; arm run.
5. 7gf.25.3, 25.7, 25.4, 7gf.5 each landed or killed with a named mechanism (one arm each, cheapest test).
Each arm: local novel number (with n) + LB (if submitted) recorded in its issue. No Kaggle slot on an unscored model.

title: All-word sentence context: OOV word windows in train/val spans, PNPL sentence ids
description:
MECHANISM (7gf.21 audit, 2026-10-02): holdout sentences are complete text: subj00_holdout01_sentence.npz = 156 sentences, 868 word slots, continuous MEG ~2.5 s each; B (gereonelvers RESULTS.md:18) reports only 451/868 are in-vocab (unverified by us; Kaggle scores in-vocab rows). Our gap check: holdout onset gaps p5/50/95 0.07/0.21/0.57 s vs our vocab-only train spans 0.08/0.29/0.83 (n=70k gaps, 60 runs) = we skip OOV words, holdout does not. Our model trains on vocab-only spans (epochs.py:89 filter, spans.py by onset gap>=0.92 s, chunk 9) so at holdout ~half the context slots are OOV windows it never saw, and local val (vocab-only) is blind to it -> plausible cause of local 0.525 vs LB 0.385. spans.py docstring 'a holdout sentence is a run of vocabulary words only' is WRONG.
DESIGN: (1) cache windows for EVERY word event (label = vocab id or OOV=-1), keep sentence index from PNPL events; (2) spans = PNPL sentences chunked to 9 words, matching holdout; (3) loss on in-vocab slots only (softmax), OOV slots context-only; optional SigLIP to per-word t5 target for OOV slots later (B trains all words); (4) val ruler = in-vocab words of novel all-word sentences (Sherlock1+TheMoth) so it SEES the holdout structure. VRAM: x now ~21 GB fp16 for vocab words; all words ~2x won't fit 32 GB -> OOV windows in pinned CPU RAM (non_blocking per batch) or decimate storage; measure word counts first.
PROOF: local all-word-context novel macro and LB move together; pre-register LB > 0.385 + 0.03.
design: STORAGE (02:45Z): don't cache overlapping windows (all words x 1 s fp16 = 24 GB; x 3 s = 72 GB, too big for VRAM). Cache each run's CONTINUOUS MEG decimated to 50 Hz in fp16 instead: sub-0 ~80 h x 3600 x 50 x 306 x 2 B ~ 8.8 GB; subjects 1-32 add ~2.6 GB. Cut windows on the GPU at batch time by gather (onset index + arange). Window length becomes a free knob (7gf.25.1), and per-window demeaning matches the holdout's Window transform. Events table per run: onset, label (ABSENT for OOV), sentenceidx.

title: LB gap audit: top Deep 0.765 / paper 73% vs our LB 0.385, local 0.525
description: Web research 2026-10-02: Deep public LB top 0.765, 20 teams >=0.66, us 0.385 (42/63). Competition paper arxiv 2609.03231: reference d'Ascoli model 73.23% BAcc@10 on comp vocab. Gap >> any knob => pipeline difference. Audit, in order: (1) holdout context reconstruction in Split.from_holdout (sentence grouping, ordering by onset, isolated rows) vs gereonelvers baseline which rebuilds full sentence for ~90% rows; (2) local-vs-LB gap 0.525->0.385: what in val differs from holdout (domain = read sentences?); (3) normalisation train vs holdout (robustness paper arxiv 2604.04129: instance norm the top generalisation factor; d'Ascoli RobustScaler + clamp 5); (4) d'Ascoli recipe: 16L/16H/1024 transformer, dedup SigLIP, t5-large mid layer. Acceptance: named mechanism for >=10 pts of the gap, or each ruled out with evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: (1) Opus diff of reference/gereonelvers pipeline vs ours written to interpretations/deep/<date>_lb_gap.md; (2) every difference mapped to an existing issue or a new one; (3) ruled-out items listed with their measurement and n.
notes:
2026-10-02T02:13Z audit: RULED OUT (a) scale/units: holdout x abs-median 1.467, chan-std median 3.81 vs Sherlock1 val 1.472/4.03 (n=960 holdout rows, 156 sentences + 92 isolated); (b) stimulus replay: onset-gap sequences of 156 holdout sentences match train/val spans exactly in 2 (1.3%), both label-ambiguous = chance; holdout sentences are novel. (c) grouping: from_holdout groups by epoch, span-len hist 1:94 3:2 4:24 5:55 6:37 7:23 8:11 9:2 = 4-9 words as expected. OPEN: model capacity/recipe vs d'Ascoli (16L/1024/dedup SigLIP), ruler domain (val=narrative, holdout=read sentences, MOCHA leaked so no read-domain ruler).
02:15Z (d) per-channel drift: holdout per-channel IQR vs each of 161 train/val runs: chan log-ratio spread p5/50/95 = 0.07/0.15/0.23, median log-ratio within +-0.2 - holdout is not a drift outlier; instance-norm deprioritised. Next: Opus diff of gereonelvers baseline (holdout 0.467) vs ours.

title: Robust-scale + clamp(5) / instance norm, identical train & holdout
description: d'Ascoli: RobustScaler per channel, clamp +-5. 2025 robustness study: instance norm most influential for val->test generalisation (39.5->61.0 F1 combined). We only remove per-window channel mean. Cheap: per-window per-channel median/IQR scale + clamp on device in batch(); no recache.
close_reason: Already present: megspeech/scaler.py Scaler = per-channel median/IQR fit on train + clamp, a model buffer applied identically to val and holdout. Instance-norm variant only if per-channel drift measured (see 7gf.21).

title: Lever: same-recipe seed ensemble (3-5 seeds)
description: Prior ensemble 0.496 mixed recipes incl. read-weight 4 (known-bad). Same-recipe seed ensembles: shipd house number +0.01-0.02. Average context-head probabilities of k seeds of the best recipe; ensemble.py exists. Bar +0.015 novel macro over best single.
notes:
2025 workshop papers: ensembling is the most consistent win - BrainWatson 5-model vote +12.7 F1 LB, Null-1 diversity ensemble +8.4 F1, SHINE 200+ models +1.4, QuantumFiremen stacker +0.5. Diverse architectures > same-recipe seeds (Null-1).
rsna_knee did many ensembles; ask that session for its recipe (stacking vs averaging, diversity source) before building.
rsna_knee recipe (02:28Z):
- Uniform LOGIT averaging; no stacking; fitted weights did not hold up.
- Supervision, not architecture, sets member correlation. Cross-architecture seats bought ~0 for them.
- WEIGHT SOUP (parent plus 3 short seed-children, weights averaged into one checkpoint) matched their 8-seat ensemble on the LB.
- Saturation at ~7 seats.
- Ensemble deltas transfer local->LB with the right sign at ~1/4 of the size.
- Rule: score an ensemble only on data no member trained on and that was not used to pick it.
Our ens-v1-rp1b was picked on the old leaky macro (0.542). On the clean novel ruler it scores 0.496 < v1 0.525, so its LB 0.310 is consistent with that; ensembling itself is not refuted.
Plan:
1. Cheap first: a soup of v1-recipe seed-children, fine-tuned from the shared parent so the weights are linearly connected.
2. Then uniform logit-average over seeds and over supervision variants (t5 CE vs SigLIP vs order clock) rather than over architectures.
CORRECTION from rsna_knee (02:29Z):
- Drop 'cross-architecture seats bought ~0'. Their champion keeps one foreign-architecture seat at a fixed 1/3 rank blend, and that seat earned its place.
- Drop the CNN -0.0025 and soup k3/k4/k7 numbers; not on their record.
- Verified and kept: supervision sets member correlation; soup alone = 8-seat ensemble = 0.946 LB; uniform weights; LB ~1.1x local delta (sd 0.0017); ensemble proxy +0.0084 -> LB +0.002; greedy-on-holdout entries voided.
Plan adjusted: after the soup, combine across supervision variants plus at most one architecture-diverse seat (e.g. multi-scale conv 7gf.26 or SSM 7gf.27).

title: Lever: GPU augmentation - onset jitter, channel dropout, gain/noise
description: Train has zero augmentation. Sibling evidence: rsna 'augmentation actually applied' +0.011 (only knob above its floor); shipd eeg_decoding has vectorised GPU aug (time shift, channel dropout p=0.4, gain lognormal+noise; train.py:34-131, mechanism only). MEG fit: word onsets carry alignment noise (forced alignment ~10-30ms) -> train-time jitter of +-1-2 samples at 50 Hz needs windows wider than 1 s (cache is exactly 1 s) so implement as circular-free shift via crop of a 1.04 s cache OR start with channel dropout + gain jitter which need no recache. Bar: novel macro +0.015 over matched arm.
notes: CAUTION 2025 papers: generic aug null (neural2speech +0.01%) or catastrophic on holdout (NTHU 21.6->3.6 F1 while test rose 44.3->47.7). Our arm ctx-order-aug40 must be judged on LB-transfer too, not local only.

title: Throughput: K arms in one process sharing the on-GPU train set
description: Training saturates neither GPU (14-20% util, 23GB VRAM) nor compute; host RAM ~18GB/run blocks a 2nd concurrent arm (box 93GB, other projects + WSL ~50GB). Audit where host RAM is held after Split.gather moves x to device (npz caches, numpy copies), drop them; then profile batch() python loop. Goal: 2-3 arms concurrent -> 2-3x arms/hour.
notes:
2026-10-02 audit: host RAM NOT the limit - WS 2.4GB; the 18-26GB figure is WDDM commit charge (commit 135/187GB, room for a 2nd run). VRAM is: train x already fp16 on GPU (306ch x 50 samples, ~21GB of 32) -> 2nd process won't fit; bf16 saves nothing. Lever = K models in ONE process sharing x (per-model seed/config, same batch draws). GPU util 14-30%. Arms ~10min/20ep so P2.
02:44Z sample: ctx-order-siglip40 runs at 12-17% GPU util, so ~5x headroom. Order of levers: (1) profile one epoch (batch python vs eval vs kernel launch); (2) K arms in one process sharing x (recipe unchanged); (3) torch.compile / bigger batch, which changes the recipe and needs a check.

title: Cross-subject pooling: holdout sentences are identical across all 40 subjects
description: Measured 2026-10-01: subj00_holdout01_sentence has 156 sentences / 155 unique onset patterns (rounded 10 ms, relative to first word); subj01 shares 155 of them. So every Deep sentence has up to 39 other-subject recordings of the same stimulus in the (Broad) holdout files. Transductive lever: match sentences by onset pattern, decode other subjects with a cross-subject model (Broad backbone / subject layer), pool log-probs per word. Plausibly large (averaging many weak decoders). NEEDS HUMAN DECISION: uses other subjects' unlabelled TEST MEG to predict Deep rows - check Kaggle rules (external data / test-data use) before building; private LB 'stimuli entirely different' may or may not repeat across subjects.
notes: 2026-10-02: Deep holdout is subject 0 only (960 rows), spread ratio to train scaler median 1.029 -> cross-subject scaling is Broad-only, not a Deep lever.

title: Sentence-context transformer over per-word CNN embeddings

title: Model recipe: replicate d'Ascoli ref (73.23%) then build past
description: Model side of the d'Ascoli reference (73.23% BAcc@10, 2609.03231 Tab1) and levers past it, on our own pipeline (megspeech.train context model). Data-side gaps live in 7gf.25; arms here run on whatever data path is current and are re-run once after 7gf.24/25.1 land if they were kept.
design:
ORDER (by expected size, cheapest test first):
1. 4te.3 SigLIP vs t5-large (running: ctx-order-siglip40).
2. 4te.2 word-index positions (ctx-order40 done: tie 0.531 vs 0.525).
3. 7gf.18 augmentation (ctx-order-aug40 queued).
4. 4te.1 context capacity toward ref 16x16x1024.
5. 7gf.19 EMA, 7gf.23 class weights/masking, 7gf.26 multi-scale conv.
6. 7gf.27 SSM, 4te.5 125 Hz (low).
Kept arms become the default TrainConfig; killed arms record the mechanism and what is NOT ruled out.
acceptance_criteria: WORK criteria: every child landed (code + tests + gates + pushed) or killed with a named mechanism; each with local novel macro + n (and LB if submitted) in its issue; kept arms merged into TrainConfig defaults and re-run once on the 7gf.25 data path.
notes:
Recipe facts (external/, read 2026-10-02): A=d'Ascoli CNN SimpleConvTimeAgg (merger 270, 1x1->512, subject layer, 5 dilated convs h160, attention pool, out 1024) -> TransformerEncoder 16x16x1024 rotary over word INDEX (no onsets); loss SigLIP vs t5-large layer12 word embeddings (CNN loss only logged); 3s window @50Hz, bandpass .1-40, RobustScaler, baseline first .5s, clamp 5; AdamW 1e-4 wd0 cosine 50ep bs128. B (gereonelvers) holdout run: A trained Sherlock1 ses1-10 only, 1s window; holdout = per-sentence 1s slices -> transformer over that sentence's vocab words; LB public 0.444 / private 0.417 (ours public 0.385). Deep holdout is subject 0 only (960 rows: 868 sentence + 92 word). Gap ~6 pts public. Arms (child issues): capacity, index positions, SigLIP-t5, Sherlock-only data.
Papers read 02:29Z.
- The d'Ascoli reference scores 73.23% BAcc@10 on the test split; the 2609.03231 table says it trained on ALL sub-0 data.
- MEG-XL fine-tuning uses 3 s windows starting 0.5 s before onset, D-SigLIP (repeated words masked) against T5-large, and time-pooling over each word span.
- Our 1 s vocab-only windows differ from the reference on both axes: window length (7gf.25.1) and coverage (7gf.24). That fits our gap: 0.385 LB vs 0.73.

value: Deep track: 5 Kaggle slots/UTC day, reset 00:00Z, last ~23:30Z, unused slots DESTROYED (never banked). Pace uniformly (rsna_knee rule, owner directive): next mark = (23:30Z - now)/slots_left, recomputed each check; no skip - a passed mark compresses later intervals, say so; never dump several at once. Cadence != gate: at a mark spend on best mechanism-backed candidate; if none beats champion, spend as INSTRUMENT (board read that retires a question, pre-registered band), labelled instrument vs improvement in description. 1.5% bar is for calling a RESULT, not for spending a slot. Our ruler transfer so far: novel macro v0 0.479->LB 0.307, ens 0.496->0.310, v1 0.525->0.385 (monotone, 3 pts). Champion = context-v1 LB 0.385. Record LB vs local in the issue.
